Note::surround¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::surround(std::string_view left, std::string_view right) const

Wrap Every Cell In A Chosen Prefix And Suffix¶

surround(left, right) returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell rewritten as left + cell + right. It is the general form of quote (surround("\"", "\"")): use it for Markdown emphasis (**...**), bracketed spans ([...]), XML-ish tags, or any fixed open/close pair.

The wrap is unconditional and literal — left and right are always added, verbatim, whether or not the cell already begins or ends with them (so surround is not idempotent), and nothing inside the cell is escaped. When you want “add it only if missing”, use ensure_prefix / ensure_suffix instead.

left and right may differ or be equal, and either may be empty (an empty right makes surround a pure prefix add). An empty cell becomes left + right. The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note.

Example 1: Brackets¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"x", "", "a]"}).surround("[", "]"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["[x]", "[]", "[a]]"]

The empty cell becomes "[]"; "a]" becomes "[a]]" — the existing ] is not deduplicated.

Example 2: The Same String On Both Sides¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"mid"}).surround("**", "**");
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["**mid**"]

Example 3: Shape Is Preserved¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({{"a", "b"}}).surround("<", ">"))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 2], dim=2, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["<a>", "<b>"]
]

See Also¶

  • Note::quote: surround("\"", "\"") with its own name.

  • Note::ensure_prefix / Note::ensure_suffix: conditional, idempotent adds.

  • Note::unquote: remove one matching pair of surrounding quote characters.
